## What "fidelity synthesized" means here, concretely

The generator produces lines shaped like `DATE TIME PID LEVEL component: message`
— the same STRUCTURAL shape as a Hadoop DataNode/NameSystem-style distributed
system log — with:

- an invented component vocabulary (`svc.BlockKeeper`, `svc.ChunkStore$Receiver`,
  …: dotted, Java-package-style, with the occasional `$InnerClass` nesting a
  real Hadoop log also has), weighted so two components dominate the traffic
  (mirroring a real DataNode log's own skew toward its busiest handlers);
- an INFO:WARN:ERROR mix of roughly 95.6% / 4.3% / 0.4% in the committed
  file (measured: `awk '{print $4}' synthetic_log_lines.txt | sort | uniq -c`
  → 7,486 / 339 / 34 of 7,859 lines);
- IPv4:port pairs, large signed decimal identifiers (roughly half negative,
  mirroring a 64-bit hash's sign bit landing either way — deliberately, since
  it puts a literal `-` inside an otherwise all-digit token, which is exactly
  the byte-frequency property that matters for this exemplar's purpose), and
  synthetic file-path-shaped tokens.

**This lane separately inspected a transient, NEVER-COMMITTED copy of
loghub's HDFS_2k.log** (fetched to `/tmp` for inspection only, deleted before
this lane's first commit, never written anywhere under this repository) —
**only** to calibrate the structural ratios above (the level mix; the rough
share of lines carrying an IP:port pair, a hash-shaped token, or a file path)
for STATISTICAL fidelity. No text, field value, component name, host, or
message string was copied from it. The component names, message templates,
hostnames and identifiers in `gen_corpus.py` are this generator's own
invention.

**Known fidelity gap, recorded rather than hidden**: `docs/design/findings/
requirements.md`'s own C4 row (line 102, from an earlier measurement against
the REAL HDFS corpus) predicts that under log-measured byte frequencies the
bench's `loglines/iso-ts` pattern moves because `-` is "3.6× commoner than
the [default] table says". This synthetic corpus does **not** reproduce that
specific finding: measured here, `ppm('-')` is 4,984 under `default.rxt` and
4,782 under this corpus's own derived table — essentially flat, not
elevated (see `docs/dev/lanes/findb5src_evidence/byte_rate_movers.py`
output). The generator's ~50%-negative chunk-identifier design was meant to
elevate `-`, and it does put a `-` in roughly half of the corpus's chunk
tokens, but not at the real corpus's own measured rate — plausibly because
real HDFS lines carry MORE such tokens per line, and/or additional dash
usage this generator does not model. **This is exactly the kind of gap a
"fidelity synthesized" label exists to disclose**: the corpus is a
structurally-plausible STAND-IN, not a byte-frequency match to any specific
real corpus, and a decision that turns on getting one byte's exact rate
right (rather than the general shape of the table) should not be taken on
this corpus's authority alone.

## Why this class ships (D123 addendum 7)

`log`/`log_lines` is one of the two FIRST shipped named analyses because it
has a measured customer: C4 (`[OPT-K]`/`[OPT-OFSK]` offset-k selection,
`requirements.md` line 102) and the `bigram`/run-rarity family once B4
lands. `json`/`prose` (`docs/dev/findings_measure/`) stay measurement
controls and are not shipped.

## Version note

Per `third_party/README.md`'s "one directory per source, version in the
name" rule, applied here to a GENERATED source exactly as to a fetched one:
changing `SEED`, `TARGET_BYTES`, or any of `gen_corpus.py`'s templates is a
deliberate, re-measured event — bump to `synth-log-lines-v2/` rather than
editing this directory's committed corpus in place.
